Ahmed al-Sharaa says Syria and Israel were “almost 90%” of the way to an agreement. Then, he says, Israel walked away and added conditions. At the UN, he answered with a familiar Syrian line: "the Golan remains Syrian territory."

He also denied any link to the September 11 attacks, saying he was 13 at the time. Public biographies, however, commonly give his birth year as 1982, which would have made him 19 in September 2001.

His Golan answer came with a joke for Donald Trump. When Trump said the Golan was under Israeli sovereignty, al-Sharaa said he replied: “Why don’t you give New Jersey to the Israelis?” Trump owns New Jersey; he does not own the Golan. The New Jersey voters, al-Sharaa added, are Democrats anyway.

At the General Assembly, al-Sharaa said the Golan “will remain Syrian land” and that Israel’s annexation measures were void under UN Security Council Resolution 497. 

He accused Israel of nearly 500 air and artillery strikes, more than 1,200 ground incursions and almost 300 arrests since Bashar al-Assad’s fall. He reaffirmed Syria’s commitment to the 1974 disengagement agreement and demanded that Israeli forces withdraw to their positions of December 8, 2024.

Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz answered that Israeli sovereignty over the Golan was permanent. He said the Hermon and the security zone had been handed to Syria under the 1974 agreement on conditions Syria later violated. 

Katz’s rule for the next round was simpler: territory Israel takes this time will remain Israeli forever, “in accordance with the laws of war.”

Al-Sharaa offers an agreement that was 90% complete. Israel answers with a map that is 100% nonnegotiable. 

The missing 10% is the territory both sides say belongs to them.
